title: Car, RV, Caravan & Boat Storage: Options Compared
description: Outdoor, covered and indoor storage for cars, motorbikes, RVs, caravans, motorhomes and boats compared, plus how to prepare a vehicle for storage.
cardText: Outdoor, covered or indoor storage for cars, RVs, caravans, motorhomes and boats.
h1: Car, RV, caravan and boat storage compared
intro: No room on the drive, a vehicle you only use in summer, or a classic you want to protect? There are several ways to store it, at very different levels of protection.

image.alt: A white caravan trailer parked on grass under a blue sky

highlights.title: Free to use
highlights.text: Our guides and comparisons cost nothing. You book directly with the storage provider.

highlights.title: Compare before you book
highlights.text: Check size, access, security and the full monthly cost, not just the headline price.

highlights.title: Home or business
highlights.text: Advice for personal storage, business storage and everything in between.

sections.html:
• Outdoor parking: a marked space in a secure, fenced yard. The most affordable option, best for vehicles built to live outdoors.
  • Covered parking: a roof but open sides. Protects from sun, rain and snow.
  • Indoor units: a fully enclosed drive-up unit. The best protection from weather and theft, often used for classic cars and motorbikes.
  • Specialist storage: some sites focus on caravans, motorhomes, boats or classic cars and offer extras like battery charging or valeting.

• Clean it inside and out, and remove food
  • Check tyre pressures, and consider moving it occasionally to avoid flat spots
  • Use a battery maintainer if the site allows, or disconnect the battery
  • Follow the manufacturer’s advice on fuel and fluids
  • Use a breathable cover
  • Remove valuables and documents

In the UK, a vehicle that is kept off public roads and isn’t taxed needs a SORN (Statutory Off Road Notification) with the DVLA. In the US, registration and insurance rules for stored vehicles vary by state. Talk to your insurer: some offer “laid-up” or storage cover, but make sure you’re covered for fire and theft while the vehicle is stored.

sections.h2: What to check at the site
sections.html:
• Security: gated access, CCTV, lighting and staff
  • Size limits for length and height, especially for RVs and boats on trailers
  • Whether you can work on the vehicle on site (most don’t allow it)
  • Access hours for weekend trips
  • Whether the site is approved by your insurer

faqs.q: Can I store a car in a regular storage unit?
faqs.a: Some facilities allow vehicles in drive-up units, usually 10 × 20 ft or larger. The vehicle often needs to be registered and insured. Check the facility’s rules first.

faqs.q: Do I need a SORN for a stored car in the UK?
faqs.a: If the vehicle isn’t taxed and is kept off public roads, you need to make a SORN with the DVLA. If it’s still taxed, a SORN isn’t needed.

faqs.q: Is indoor or outdoor RV storage better?
faqs.a: Indoor storage protects against sun, weather and theft but costs more and is harder to find for large RVs. Covered parking is a common middle ground.
